1.1: There was a wise man, a skilled craftsman, whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 loved and received, so that he might witness the highest dwellings and the wise, great, incomprehensible, and unchanging realm of Elohim Almighty. He was to behold the wondrous, esteemed, radiant, many-eyed ranks of the servants of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, His unapproachable throne, the ranks and manifestations of the bodiless hosts, the indescribable service of the multitude of elements, the varied appearances and inexpressible songs of the keruḇim, and the boundless light.
1.2: At that time, he said, “When I had completed one hundred and sixty-five years, I became the father of my son Methushelaḥ.”
1.3: Afterward I lived another two hundred years, making all the years of my life three hundred and sixty-five.
1.4: On the first day of the month, I was alone in my house, resting on my bed, and fell asleep.
1.5: While I slept, great distress filled my heart, and I wept in my sleep. I could not understand the cause of my distress or what was going to happen to me.
1.6: Then two men appeared to me, greater in stature than anyone I had ever seen on earth. Their faces shone like the sun, their eyes burned like flames, and fire came from their lips. Their clothing was purple in appearance, and their singing was varied. Their wings were brighter than gold, and their hands were whiter than snow.
1.7: They stood at the head of my bed and began calling me by name.
1.8: I awoke and clearly saw the two men standing before me.
1.9: I greeted them, but fear seized me, and my face changed with terror. Then the men said to me:
1.10: “Be courageous, Ḥanoḵ, and do not fear. The eternal Elohim has sent us to you. Today you shall ascend with us into the shamayim. Tell your sons and everyone in your household what they must do on earth in your absence, and let no one search for you until 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 returns you to them.”
1.11: I hurried to obey them, went out of my house, and approached the doors as they had instructed me. I summoned my sons Methushelaḥ, Regim, and Gaidad, and told them all the wonders the men had revealed to me.

10.1: The two men led me toward the north and showed me a terrifying place filled with every kind of torment. There was harsh darkness and impenetrable gloom, with no light except a murky fire that continually blazed upward. A river of fire flowed through it. Fire was everywhere, yet so were frost, ice, thirst, and shivering. The bonds were cruel, and the messenger-spirits were frightening and merciless, carrying weapons of punishment. Then I said:
10.2: “Woe, woe! How terrifying this place is!”
10.3: The men answered, “This place, Ḥanoḵ, is prepared for those who dishonor 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄: those who commit unnatural acts, including the sexual corruption of children; those who practice sorcery, enchantments, and wicked witchcraft; and those who boast of their evil deeds. It is for thieves, liars, slanderers, the envious and resentful, those who commit sexual immorality and murder, and those who steal the lives of others. It is for those who take from the poor to enrich themselves, who could feed the hungry but let them die, and who could clothe the naked but instead strip them. They did not acknowledge their Creator but bowed to lifeless and powerless mighty ones that cannot see or hear. They made carved images and worshiped the unclean work of their own hands. For all such people, this place is prepared as an everlasting inheritance.”

11.1: The men led me into the fourth shamayim and showed me the movements and rays of light of the sun and moon.
11.2: I measured their courses, compared their light, and saw that the sun shines more brightly than the moon.
11.3: I saw the sun's circle and the wheels on which it travels. It moves with remarkable speed, like a passing wind, and has no rest by day or night.
11.4: Four great stars accompany its departure and return, each with a thousand stars beneath it, on the right side of the sun's wheel. Four more are on the left, each also with a thousand stars, making eight thousand stars that continually go forth with the sun.
11.5: By day, fifteen myriads of messengers accompany it, and by night, a thousand.
11.6: Six-winged beings go out with the messengers before the sun's wheel into the blazing flames, and a hundred messengers kindle the sun and set it alight.

12.1: I looked and saw other flying beings associated with the sun, called Phoenixes and Chalkydri. They were extraordinary, with feet and tails like those of lions and heads like crocodiles. Their color was purple like a rainbow. They were nine hundred measures in size, and each had twelve wings resembling those of messengers. They attended and accompanied the sun, carrying heat and dew as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded them.
12.2: Thus the sun moves in its circle and rises beneath the shamayim. Its course continues beneath the earth, and its rays shine without ceasing.

13.1: The men carried me eastward and placed me at the gates of the sun, where it comes forth according to the seasons, the cycle of the months of the whole year, and the number of hours in day and night.
13.2: I saw six open gates, each measuring sixty-one and a quarter stadia. I measured them carefully and confirmed their size. Through these gates the sun goes forth, travels westward, becomes balanced, and rises throughout the months. It then returns through the six gates according to the succession of the seasons. In this way the yearly cycle is completed through the four seasons.

14.1: The men took me to the west and showed me six great open gates corresponding to those in the east. There the sun sets according to the count of three hundred and sixty-five and a quarter days.
14.2: The sun descends through the western gates, withdrawing its great brightness beneath the earth. Its crown of radiance remains in the shamayim with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, guarded by four hundred messengers. While the sun travels beneath the earth on its wheel, it remains there for seven great hours of the night and spends half its course below. In the eighth hour of the night it approaches the east, takes up its light and radiant crown, and shines forth more fiercely than fire.

15.1: Then the beings of the sun, called Phoenixes and Chalkydri, break into song. At the command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, every bird flutters its wings and rejoices in the giver of light.
15.2: The giver of light comes to brighten the whole world. The morning watch appears with the sun's rays, and the sun goes forth over the earth, receiving its brightness to illuminate the entire earth. The men showed me how the sun's course is calculated.
15.3: The gates through which the sun passes are the great gates by which the hours of the year are counted. The sun is a great creation, and its cycle lasts twenty-eight years before beginning again.

16.1: The men also showed me the course of the moon, with twelve great gates arranged from west to east. Through them the moon comes and goes at its appointed times.
16.2: It passes through the first western gate of the sun for exactly thirty-one days; through the second for thirty-one days; the third for thirty; the fourth for thirty; the fifth for thirty-one; the sixth for thirty-one; the seventh for thirty; the eighth for thirty-one; the ninth for thirty-one; the tenth for thirty; the eleventh for thirty-one; and the twelfth for twenty-eight days.
16.3: It passes through the western gates in the same order and number as the eastern gates, completing the three hundred and sixty-five and a quarter days of the solar year. The lunar year has three hundred and fifty-four days, falling short of the solar cycle by twelve days, called the lunar epacts of the whole year.
16.4: The great cycle also contains five hundred and thirty-two years.
16.5: The quarter-day is left out for three years, and in the fourth year it is accounted for in full.
16.6: For three years those portions are left outside the reckoning of the shamayim and are not added to the count of days, because they cause the years to vary, with two months increasing toward completion and two others decreasing.
16.7: When the course through the western gates is complete, the moon returns toward the eastern gates and their lights. It travels day and night around the circles of the shamayim, beneath all the other circles and swifter than the winds of the shamayim, the spirits, the elements, and the flying messengers. Each messenger has six wings.
16.8: Its course completes seven cycles in nineteen years.

17.1: In the midst of the shamayim I saw armed hosts serving 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with drums and musical instruments. Their voices rose in unceasing, sweet, and varied songs too wonderful to describe, astonishing everyone who heard them. I delighted in the singing of those messengers.

18.1: The men took me into the fifth shamayim. There I saw countless watchers called Grigori. They looked like men but were larger than great giants. Their faces were withered, their mouths remained silent, and no service was offered in the fifth shamayim. I asked the men who accompanied me:
18.2: “Why are their faces so withered and sorrowful? Why are their mouths silent, and why is there no service in this shamayim?”
18.3: They answered, “These are the Grigori, who, together with their prince Satanail, rejected 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Those held in deep darkness in the second shamayim belong to their company. Three of them descended to earth from the throne of the Meleḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to Mount Ḥermon. There they broke their vows upon the slopes of Ḥermon, saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and took wives for themselves. They defiled the earth through their deeds, spreading lawlessness and forbidden unions throughout their days. Giants were born, men of extraordinary size, and great hostility arose.”
18.4: Therefore Elohim judged them severely. They weep for their brothers, and they too will be punished on the great day of the Meleḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
18.5: I said to the Grigori, “I have seen your brothers, their deeds, and their great torments. I prayed for them, but the Meleḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has condemned them to remain beneath the earth until the present shamayim and earth come to an end.”
18.6: I said, “Why do you wait, brothers, instead of serving before the face of the Meleḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄? Why have you not offered your service before Him, so that you do not provoke 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to anger?”
18.7: They listened to my warning and spoke to the four ranks in the shamayim. As I stood with the two men, four trumpets sounded together with a mighty voice. The Grigori began singing in unison, and their voices rose sorrowfully and earnestly before the Meleḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

19.1: From there the men carried me into the sixth shamayim. I saw seven companies of messengers, radiant and esteemed, their faces shining more brightly than the sun. They were alike in appearance, conduct, and clothing. They establish the appointed orders and study the movements of the stars, the changes of the moon, the course of the sun, and the proper governance of the world.
19.2: When they see wrongdoing, they issue commands and instructions, and they sing sweetly and loudly, offering every kind of song of praise.
19.3: These are the chief messengers who oversee the other messengers and measure all life in the shamayim and on earth. Some are appointed over seasons and years; others over rivers and seas, the fruit of the earth, and every plant that provides food for living creatures. Others record the lives, deeds, and beings of mankind before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Among them are six Phoenixes, six keruḇim, and six six-winged beings. They sing continually with one voice, and their song cannot be described. They rejoice before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at His footstool.

2.1: “Listen to me, my children. I do not know where I am going or what will happen to me. Therefore, do not turn away from Elohim to worthless mighty ones that did not make the shamayim and the earth. They and those who worship them will perish. May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 strengthen your hearts in reverence for Him. And now, my children, let no one try to find me until 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 returns me to you.”

20.1: The two men lifted me into the seventh shamayim. There I saw an exceedingly great light, fiery companies of mighty chief messengers, bodiless powers, dominions, orders and authorities, keruḇim, seraphim, thrones, many-eyed beings, nine ranks, and the Ioanit stations of light. I trembled in great fear. The men led me onward and said:
20.2: “Be courageous, Ḥanoḵ, and do not fear.” They showed me 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from a distance, seated upon His lofty throne. For what is in the tenth shamayim, where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 dwells?
20.3: Elohim is in the tenth shamayim, which is called Aravoth in the Hebrew tongue.
20.4: All the hosts of the shamayim come and stand upon the ten steps according to their ranks. They bow before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, then return joyfully to their places, singing softly and tenderly in the boundless light as they serve Him in esteem.

21.1: The keruḇim and seraphim around the throne, the six-winged and many-eyed beings, never depart. They stand before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, doing His will and surrounding His throne. With gentle voices they sing, “Qadosh, qadosh, qadosh! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the shamayim and the earth are full of Your esteem.”
21.2: When I saw all this, the men said to me, “Ḥanoḵ, we have been commanded to accompany you only this far.” Then they departed, and I did not see them again.
21.3: I remained alone at the edge of the seventh shamayim. Fear seized me, and I fell on my face and said to myself, “Woe is me! What has happened to me?”
21.4: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent one of His esteemed ones, the chief messenger Gaḇri’ĕl, who said to me, “Be courageous, Ḥanoḵ, and do not fear. Rise and come with me to stand before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 forever.”
21.5: I answered him in my heart, “My master, fear and trembling have nearly taken my life. I depended upon the men who brought me here, and I expected to go with them before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
21.6: Gaḇri’ĕl lifted me as the wind lifts a leaf and placed me before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
21.7: I saw the eighth shamayim, called Muzaloth in Hebrew. It governs the changes of seasons, drought and rain, and the twelve constellations of the circle of the firmament above the seventh shamayim.
21.8: I saw the ninth shamayim, called Kuchavim in Hebrew, where the dwellings of the shamayim of the twelve constellations of the firmament are found.

22.1: In the tenth shamayim, called Aravoth, I saw the appearance of the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, like iron heated until it glows and then drawn from the fire, throwing off burning sparks.
22.2: For an instant in eternity I saw the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. His face is beyond description, marvelous, awe-inspiring, and exceedingly fearsome.
22.3: Who am I to describe the indescribable being of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 or His wondrous face? I cannot count His many instructions or the varied voices around Him. His throne is immense and not made by human hands. I cannot count the hosts of keruḇim and seraphim standing around Him or describe their ceaseless singing, His unchanging beauty, or the unspeakable greatness of His esteem.
22.4: I fell facedown and bowed before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and He said to me:
22.5: “Be courageous, Ḥanoḵ, and do not fear. Rise and stand before My face forever.”
22.6: The chief commander Miḵa’ĕl lifted me up and brought me before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.7: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to His servants, testing them, “Let Ḥanoḵ stand before Me forever.” The esteemed ones bowed before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and said, “Let Ḥanoḵ go according to Your word.”
22.8: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Miḵa’ĕl, “Remove Ḥanoḵ’s earthly garments, anoint him with My fragrant oil, and clothe him in the garments of My esteem.”
22.9: Miḵa’ĕl did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded. He anointed and clothed me. The ointment shone more brightly than the great light, was like sweet dew, and had a gentle fragrance. It gleamed like a ray of sunlight. When I looked at myself, I had been transformed and appeared like one of His esteemed ones.
22.10: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 summoned one of His chief messengers named Pravuil, whose wisdom and understanding surpassed those of the other chief messengers and who recorded all the deeds of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. He said to Pravuil, “Bring the books from My treasuries and a reed for swift writing. Give them to Ḥanoḵ, and place the chosen books of encouragement into his hands.”

23.1: He told me about all the works of the shamayim, the earth, and the sea; all the elements and their movements; the thunder and its sound; the sun, moon, and changing courses of the stars; the seasons, years, days, and hours; the rising of the winds; the number of messengers and the ordering of their songs; and all the matters of mankind, their languages, songs, and lives. He taught me commands, instructions, and sweet songs, and everything I needed to learn.
23.2: Pravuil said to me, “We have written down everything I have told you. Sit and write about the beings of mankind, however many are born, and the places prepared for them forever. For all beings were prepared before the foundation of the world.”
23.3: For twice thirty days and thirty nights I wrote everything down carefully, filling three hundred and sixty-six books.

24.1: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 summoned me and said, “Ḥanoḵ, sit at My left side with Gaḇri’ĕl.”
24.2: I bowed before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and He said to me, “Beloved Ḥanoḵ, I will tell you about all the things you see standing complete, even as they were before the very beginning: everything I created from nonexistence, and visible things from what is invisible and spiritual.”
24.3: “Listen, Ḥanoḵ, and take My words to heart. I have not revealed My secret to My messengers. I have not told them how they came into being or revealed My endless realm to them. They have not understood My work of creation, which I now reveal to you.”
24.4: “Before anything visible and physical existed, I alone moved among the invisible and spiritual things, as the sun travels from east to west and west to east.”
24.5: “Even the sun has rest in itself, but I found no rest, for I was creating all things. I planned to lay foundations and bring visible, physical creation into being.”

25.1: “I commanded that visible things should come forth from the invisible depths. Then Adoil descended, immense in size, and I saw that his body was filled with great light.”
25.2: “I said to him, ‘Open yourself, Adoil, and let the visible creation come out of you.’”
25.3: “He opened, and a great light came forth. I stood in the midst of that light. As light came forth from light, a great age emerged, revealing all the creation I had planned to make.”
25.4: “And I saw that it was good.”
25.5: “I established a throne for Myself and sat upon it. I said to the light, ‘Rise higher and establish yourself above the throne, becoming a foundation for the things above.’”
25.6: “Nothing exists above that light. Then I rose and looked upward from My throne.”

26.1: “I called into the lowest depths a second time and said, ‘Let Archas come forth, solid and firm.’ And he came forth from the invisible realm.”
26.2: “Archas appeared, hard, heavy, and very red.”
26.3: “I said, ‘Open yourself, Archas, and let what is within you be born.’ He opened, and a vast, dark age came forth, bearing the creation of all the lower things. I saw that it was good and said to him:”
26.4: “‘Go down below, make yourself firm, and become the foundation for the lower things.’ He went down and established himself as their foundation. Nothing exists below that darkness.”

27.1: “I commanded that something be taken from light and darkness, and said, ‘Become dense.’ And so it became dense. I spread it out with the light, and it became water. I extended it above the darkness and beneath the light. I made the waters firm, forming the bottomless deep, and placed a foundation of light around the water. I formed seven circles within it and shaped the water like crystal, both wet and dry, like glass. I established the circuits of the waters and the other elements, showing each its appointed path, and assigned each of the seven stars its own shamayim. I saw that it was good.”
27.2: “I separated the light from the darkness in the midst of the waters, on one side and the other. I commanded the light to be day and the darkness to be night. And there was evening and there was morning, the first day.”

28.1: “Then I made the circle of the shamayim firm and commanded the lower waters beneath it to gather together in one place and the dry land to appear. And it happened as I commanded.”
28.2: “From the waves I made great, solid rock. From the rock I raised the dry land, calling it earth. I called the depths of the earth the abyss, the bottomless deep. I gathered the sea into one place and bound it within its limits.”
28.3: “I said to the sea, ‘Behold, I have given you your everlasting boundaries, and you shall not break beyond them.’”
28.4: “Thus I established the firmament. I called this the first-created day.”

29.1: “I formed the image and nature of fire for all the hosts of the shamayim. My eye looked upon the exceedingly hard rock, and from the flash of My eye lightning received its wondrous nature: fire within water and water within fire. Neither puts out the other nor dries the other up. Therefore lightning is brighter than the sun, softer than water, and firmer than hard rock.”
29.2: “From the rock I cut off a great fire, and from the fire I created the ten orders of bodiless hosts of messengers. Their weapons were fiery, their garments were burning flames, and I commanded each to stand in his appointed order.”
29.3: “One of the messengers turned away with those under his command and conceived an impossible thought: to place his throne higher than the clouds above the earth and make himself equal in rank to My power.”
29.4: “I cast him down from the heights with his messengers, and he continued to fly through the air above the bottomless deep.”

3.1: When Ḥanoḵ had spoken to his sons, the messengers lifted him onto their wings and carried him into the first shamayim, setting him upon the clouds. I looked around, then looked upward and saw the upper air. They showed me an immense sea in the first shamayim, greater than any sea on earth.

30.1: “On the third day I commanded the earth to bring forth great, fruitful trees, hills, and seed-bearing plants. I planted paradise, enclosed it, and appointed flaming messengers to guard it. Thus I brought forth new growth.”
30.2: “Then evening came and morning came, the fourth day.”
30.3: “On the fourth day I commanded great lights to appear in the circles of the shamayim.”
30.4: “On the highest circle I placed Kruno; on the second, Aphrodit; on the third, Aris; on the fourth, the sun; on the fifth, Zoues; on the sixth, Ermis; and on the seventh and lowest circle, the moon. I adorned the lower region with the lesser stars.”
30.5: “On the lower circle I placed the sun to light the day and the moon and stars to light the night.”
30.6: “I appointed the sun to travel through the twelve constellations and established the order of the months, their names and durations, their thunderings, and their divisions into hours.”
30.7: “Then evening came and morning came, the fifth day.”
30.8: “On the fifth day I commanded the sea to bring forth fish, birds of many kinds, creatures that creep upon the earth, animals that walk on four legs, creatures that soar through the air, male and female, and every being that breathes the spirit of life.”
30.9: “Then evening came and morning came, the sixth day.”
30.10: “On the sixth day I commanded My wisdom to create man from seven substances: first, his flesh from the earth; second, his blood from the dew; third, his eyes from the sun; fourth, his bones from stone; fifth, his understanding from the swiftness of the messengers and from the clouds; sixth, his veins and hair from the grass of the earth; and seventh, his being from My breath and from the wind.”
30.11: “I gave him seven faculties: hearing through his flesh, sight through his eyes, smell through his being, touch through his veins, taste through his blood, endurance through his bones, and enjoyment through his understanding.”
30.12: “I conceived a subtle saying: I made man from invisible spiritual nature and visible physical nature. From both arise his life, death, and image. He has the gift of speech, though he is a created being, small in greatness and great in smallness. I placed him on earth as a second messenger, honorable, great, and esteemed. I appointed him to rule the earth and possess My wisdom. No other creature on earth was like him.”
30.13: “I gave him a name drawn from the four directions: east, west, south, and north. I appointed four special stars for him and called him Aḏam. I showed him the two ways, light and darkness, and said:”
30.14: “‘This is good, and that is evil,’ so that it might become clear whether he loved or hated Me, and which of his descendants would love Me.”
30.15: “I knew his nature, but he did not know his own. Because of his lack of understanding he would sin all the more. And I said, ‘What remains after sin except death?’”
30.16: “I caused him to fall into a deep sleep. I took one of his ribs and made a wife for him, through whom death would come to him. From his last word I called her ‘mother,’ that is, Ḥawwah.”

31.1: “Aḏam had life on earth, and I created a garden in Ĕḏen, toward the east, where he was to observe the covenant and keep the command.”
31.2: “I opened the shamayim to him so that he could see the messengers singing their song of victory and behold the light without darkness.”
31.3: “He remained in paradise, but the evil one understood that I intended to create another world and that Aḏam had been appointed to govern the earth.”
31.4: “The evil one is the wicked spirit of the lower places. After fleeing from the shamayim, Satanail was also called Sotona. He became separated from the messengers, yet his understanding of righteousness and sin remained.”
31.5: “He understood his condemnation and the sin he had committed. Therefore he plotted against Aḏam, entered in that form, and deceived Ḥawwah, but did not touch Aḏam.”
31.6: “I cursed ignorance, but I did not curse those to whom I had previously shown favor. I did not curse man, the earth, or the other creatures, but the evil fruit of man's deeds.”

32.1: “I said to him, ‘You are earth, and to the earth from which I took you, you shall return. I will not destroy you, but send you back to the place from which I took you.’”
32.2: “‘Then I shall receive you again at My second appearance.’”
32.3: “I baraḵ all My creatures, both visible and invisible. And Aḏam remained in paradise for five and a half hours.”
32.4: “I baraḵ the seventh day, the Shabbath, on which I rested from all My works.”

33.1: “I also appointed the eighth day, the first day after My work, so that the first seven would unfold in the pattern of seven thousand years. At the beginning of the eighth thousand there would be a timeless age without end, with no years, months, weeks, days, or hours.”
33.2: “And now, Ḥanoḵ, everything I have told you, everything you have understood and seen in the shamayim and on earth, and everything written in the books through My great wisdom, I conceived and created from the highest foundation to the lowest and to the very end. No one counseled Me, and no one inherits My work of creation.”
33.3: “I am eternal of Myself, not made by hands, and unchanging.”
33.4: “My thought is My counselor. My wisdom and My word are made, and My eyes watch all things as they stand here trembling in fear.”
33.5: “If I turn away My face, everything will be destroyed.”
33.6: “Pay attention, Ḥanoḵ, and know the One who speaks to you. Take the books you have written.”
33.7: “I give you Samuil and Raḡu’ĕl, who brought you here, together with the books. Go down to the earth and tell your sons everything I have told you and everything you have seen, from the lowest shamayim to My throne and all its hosts.”
33.8: “For I created all powers. None can resist Me or refuse to submit to Me. All are subject to My authority and serve under My rule alone.”
33.9: “Give your sons the books you have written. They shall read them and know that I am the Creator of all things, and understand that there is no other Elohim besides Me.”
33.10: “Let them pass on your written books from children to children, generation to generation, and nation to nation.”
33.11: “I shall give you My intercessor, the chief commander Miḵa’ĕl, concerning the writings of your ancestors Aḏam, Shĕth, Enosh, Qĕynan, Mahalal’ĕl, and your father Yereḏ.”

34.1: “They have rejected My commands and My yoke. A worthless generation has arisen, without fear of Elohim. They refuse to bow before Me and instead worship worthless elohim. They deny My oneness and fill the earth with lies, offenses, shameful sexual immorality with one another, and every other kind of uncleanness and wickedness too shameful to describe.”
34.2: “Therefore I shall bring a great flood upon the earth and destroy all mankind, and the whole earth shall be plunged into great darkness.”

35.1: “Behold, much later another generation shall arise from their descendants, but many among them shall be insatiable.”
35.2: “The one who raises up that generation shall reveal to them the books written by you and your ancestors. He shall entrust the care of the world to faithful people who do what pleases Me and do not treat My Name as something empty.”
35.3: “They shall tell another generation, and those who read the books in later times shall receive greater esteem than the first.”

36.1: “Now, Ḥanoḵ, I give you thirty days to remain in your house. Tell your sons and everyone in your household what you have heard from Me, so that all may read and understand that there is no other Elohim besides Me.”
36.2: “Let them always keep My commands and begin to read and understand the books you have written.”
36.3: “After thirty days I shall send My messenger to take you from the earth and from your sons and bring you to Me.”

37.1: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 called one of the senior messengers, a fearsome and commanding figure, and placed him beside me. He was as white as snow, and his hands were like ice, covered with the appearance of heavy frost. He cooled my face, for I could not bear the awe of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, just as a man cannot endure the blazing heat of a furnace or the sun, or the bitter cold of the air.
37.2: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “Ḥanoḵ, unless your face is cooled here, no man will be able to look upon it.”

38.1: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to the men who had first carried me upward, “Take Ḥanoḵ down to the earth with you and wait with him until the appointed day.”
38.2: They returned me to my bed during the night.
38.3: Methushelaḥ had been waiting for me, keeping watch beside my bed day and night. He was filled with awe when he heard that I had returned. I told him, “Gather everyone in my household so that I may tell them everything.”

39.1: “My children, my beloved ones, hear your father's instruction, which is according to the will of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
39.2: “I have been permitted to return to you today to announce, not from my own lips but from the lips of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, all that was, all that is, and all that shall be until the day of judgment.”
39.3: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has allowed me to return to you. Listen, then, to the words of my lips. You see me as a man of great stature among you, but I have seen the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, like iron glowing in the fire, sending forth sparks and burning.”
39.4: “You look into my eyes, the eyes of a man you consider great, but I have seen the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, shining like the rays of the sun and filling mankind with awe.”
39.5: “You see my right hand helping you, my children, but I have seen the right hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 filling the shamayim as He helped me.”
39.6: “You see the extent of my work, which is like your own, but I have seen the boundless and perfect extent of the work of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which has no end.”
39.7: “You hear the words of my lips, but I have heard the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, sounding like mighty, unceasing thunder among rushing clouds.”
39.8: “Now, my children, hear the words of the father of the earth. How fearsome it is to stand before an earthly ruler! How much more awesome it is to stand before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Judge of the living and the dead and of all the hosts of the shamayim. Who can endure that endless suffering?”

4.1: They brought the elders and rulers of the orders of stars before me and showed me two hundred messengers who govern the stars and their service in the shamayim. They fly on their wings and travel around those who sail.

40.1: “Now, my children, I know all these things, for I heard them from the lips of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and saw them with my own eyes, from beginning to end.”
40.2: “I have written in books all that I know: the shamayim, their boundaries, their fullness, and all their hosts and movements.”
40.3: “I measured and described the stars in all their countless multitude.”
40.4: “What man has seen their courses and the gates through which they enter? Not even the messengers know their number, yet I have written down all their names.”
40.5: “I measured the sun's circle and its rays and counted the hours. I recorded everything that moves upon the earth, every living thing that is nourished, every seed sown and unsown that the earth brings forth, every plant, blade of grass, and flower, together with their names and sweet fragrances. I also recorded the dwelling places of the clouds, their forms and wings, and how they carry rain and release its drops.”
40.6: “I examined everything and wrote about the paths of thunder and lightning. I was shown their keys and guardians, where they arise, and how they travel. They are released gently and in measured amounts, as though restrained by a chain, so that they do not break forth violently, drive the storm clouds down, and destroy everything on earth.”
40.7: “I recorded the treasuries of snow, the storehouses of cold and freezing air, and the keeper of their appointed times. He fills the clouds from these stores without exhausting them.”
40.8: “I wrote about the resting places of the winds. I saw their keepers carrying scales and measuring weights, placing them first on one side and then on the other, and releasing the winds carefully over the whole earth. Thus their powerful breath does not shake the earth.”
40.9: “I measured the whole earth: its mountains, hills, fields, trees, stones, rivers, and everything that exists. I recorded the height from the earth to the seventh shamayim and the depths below to the lowest place of torment, the place of judgment, that vast, open realm filled with weeping.”
40.10: “I saw the prisoners suffering there as they awaited the boundless judgment.”
40.11: “I recorded all who stood before the Judge, their judgments, their sentences, and their deeds.”

41.1: I saw all the ancestors from every age, including Aḏam and Ḥawwah. I sighed, burst into tears, and lamented their ruin and dishonor.
41.2: “Woe to me for my weakness and the weakness of my ancestors!” I thought within my heart and said:
41.3: “Ashrĕ is the man who has never been born, or who has been born and does not sin before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, so that he will not enter this place or bear its yoke.”

42.1: I saw the keepers of the keys and the guards standing at the gates of the place of torment. They were like great serpents, their faces like lamps going out, with fiery eyes and sharp teeth. I saw that all the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are right, while the works of mankind are sometimes good and sometimes evil. By their deeds those who act deceitfully are made known.

43.1: “My children, I measured and recorded every work, every measure, and every righteous judgment.”
43.2: “As one year may be more esteemed than another, so one person may be more honored than another: some for great possessions, some for wisdom, some for understanding or skill, others for restraint in speech, purity, strength, beauty, youth, quick thinking, appearance, or sensitivity. Yet hear this everywhere: none is greater than the one who fears 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. That person shall be more highly esteemed in the age to come.”

44.1: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made mankind with His own hands and in the likeness of His face. He made man both small and great.
44.2: Whoever insults the face of an earthly ruler and despises the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has treated 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with contempt. Whoever vents anger against a person who has done no wrong shall be struck down by the great anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Whoever spits contemptuously in another person's face shall be condemned at the great judgment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
44.3: Ashrĕ is the man who harbors no malice against anyone, helps those who are injured or condemned, lifts up the broken, and gives to the needy. On the day of the great judgment, every weight and measure shall be displayed as openly as goods weighed in a marketplace. Each person shall know his own measure and receive his reward accordingly.

45.1: Whoever eagerly brings an offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall find that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 acts swiftly in response to his work.
45.2: But whoever adds to the light of his lamp before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 yet fails to judge rightly shall not have his treasure increased by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in the highest realm.
45.3: If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 were to demand bread, lamps, the flesh of animals, or any other sacrifice, these things would be nothing in themselves. Elohim requires pure hearts and uses such things to test the human heart.

46.1: “Hear me, my people, and take my words to heart.”
46.2: “If anyone brings gifts to an earthly ruler while secretly harboring disloyalty, and the ruler knows it, will he not become angry, reject the gifts, and hand that person over for judgment?”
46.3: “Likewise, if a man deceives another with flattering words while concealing evil in his heart, will the other not recognize his treachery? The deceiver will be condemned, for his falsehood will become plain to all.”
46.4: “When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sends a great light, the righteous and the unrighteous alike shall face judgment, and no one will escape His notice.”

47.1: “Now, my children, take these matters to heart and pay close attention to your father's words, which came to you from the lips of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
47.2: “Take these books written by your father and read them.”
47.3: “For they are many, and through them you will learn all the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, from the beginning of creation to the end of time.”
47.4: “If you keep what I have written, you will not sin against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. There is none besides 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, whether in the shamayim, on the earth, in the lowest depths, or in the foundations beneath.”
47.5: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has laid foundations in places unknown and stretched out the visible and invisible shamayim. He established the earth upon the waters and made countless creatures. Who has counted the waters and the foundations of what has no fixed support, the dust of the earth, the sand of the sea, the raindrops, the morning dew, or the breaths of the wind? Who has filled the earth and sea and established the unyielding winter?”
47.6: “I cut the stars from fire, adorned the shamayim, and set them in their places.”

48.1: The sun travels through the seven circles of the shamayim. There are one hundred and eighty-two appointed stations for its descent toward the shortest day and another one hundred and eighty-two toward the longest day. It has two resting places and moves back and forth above the stations of the months. From the seventeenth day of Tsivan it descends toward the month Thevan, and from the seventeenth day of Thevan it rises again.
48.2: When the sun draws near the earth, the earth rejoices and brings forth fruit. When it moves away, the earth grows sorrowful, and the trees and fruits cease to blossom.
48.3: He measured all this precisely, determining the hours and establishing their measure through His wisdom, for both visible and invisible things.
48.4: From what is invisible and spiritual He made all things visible and physical, although He Himself remains invisible.
48.5: “Therefore, my children, I make these things known to you. Pass these books on to your children throughout your generations and to nations willing to fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Let them receive the books, love them more than food or earthly delights, read them, and devote themselves to their teaching.”
48.6: “But those who do not know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who do not fear Elohim, and who reject the books rather than receive them shall face a fearful judgment.”
48.7: “Ashrĕ is the man who bears their burden and carries them forward, for he shall be set free on the day of the great judgment.”

49.1: “My children, I assure you of these things without swearing an oath by the shamayim, the earth, or any other creature Elohim has made.”
49.2: “The Meleḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, ‘There is no oath or injustice in Me, only truth.’”
49.3: “Where truth is lacking among men, let them speak simply: ‘Yes, yes,’ or ‘No, no.’”
49.4: “I tell you with certainty that no one has ever been conceived in his mother's womb without a place of rest already prepared for his being and a measure appointed for the trials he will face in this world.”
49.5: “Yes, children, do not deceive yourselves, for a place has already been prepared for every human being.”

5.1: I looked down and saw the treasuries of snow, the messengers guarding those fearsome storehouses, and the clouds from which they emerge and into which they return.

50.1: “I have recorded the deeds of every person, and no one born on earth, nor any of their works, can remain hidden.”
50.3: “Therefore, my children, live your days with patience and gentleness so that you may inherit everlasting life.”
50.4: “Endure every wound, insult, evil word, and attack for the sake of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
50.5: “If anyone repays you with evil, do not repay your neighbor or enemy in the same way. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall repay them and be your avenger on the day of the great judgment, so do not seek revenge among men.”
50.6: “Whoever spends gold or silver to help a brother shall receive abundant treasure in the age to come.”
50.7: “Do not harm widows, orphans, or strangers, lest the wrath of Elohim come upon you.”

51.1: “Extend your hands to the poor according to your ability.”
51.2: “Do not hide your silver in the earth.”
51.3: “Help a faithful person in distress, and distress shall not overcome you in your own time of trouble.”
51.4: “Bear every heavy and cruel burden that comes upon you for the sake of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and you shall receive your reward on the day of judgment.”
51.5: “It is good to enter the dwelling of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in the morning, at midday, and in the evening, giving esteem to your Creator.”
51.6: “For everything that breathes esteems Him, and every visible and invisible creature offers Him praise.”

52.1: “Ashrĕ is the man who opens his lips to praise the Elohim of hosts and honors 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from his heart.”
52.2: “Cursed is the man who uses his lips to insult and slander his neighbor, for in doing so he shows contempt for Elohim.”
52.3: “Ashrĕ is the one who opens his lips to baraḵ and praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
52.4: “The one who speaks curses and abuse is cursed before the Meleḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 throughout his days.”
52.5: “Ashrĕ is the one who speaks well of all the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
52.6: “Cursed is the one who treats the creation of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with contempt.”
52.7: “Ashrĕ is the one who looks upon the fallen and raises them up.”
52.8: “Cursed is the one who eagerly seeks the destruction of what belongs to another.”
52.9: “Ashrĕ is the one who holds fast to the foundations established by the ancestors from the beginning.”
52.10: “Cursed is the one who twists the decrees of the ancestors.”
52.11: “Ashrĕ is the one who brings peace and love.”
52.12: “Cursed is the one who disturbs those who love their neighbors.”
52.13: “Ashrĕ is the one who speaks to everyone with humility of heart and tongue.”
52.14: “Cursed is the one who speaks peace with his lips while hiding a sword in his heart.”
52.15: “For all these things shall be exposed on the scales and in the books on the day of the great judgment.”

53.1: “Now, my children, do not say, ‘Our father stands before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and prays for our sins.’ For there is no helper there for anyone who has sinned.”
53.2: “You have seen how I recorded the deeds of every person before that person was created, and everything mankind would do throughout all generations. No one can fully describe all that I have written, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sees every thought of mankind, including the empty and deceptive thoughts hidden in the treasuries of the heart.”
53.3: “Now, my children, pay close attention to all the words I have spoken, so that you will not later regret and say, ‘Why did our father not tell us?’”

54.1: “If at that time you do not understand these things, let the books I have given you remain an inheritance of peace for you.”
54.2: “Give them to everyone who desires them, and instruct those people, so that they may see the great and wondrous works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”

55.1: “My children, behold, the end of my appointed time has drawn near.”
55.2: “The messengers who will accompany me are standing before me, urging me to depart from you. They are here on earth, awaiting the command given to them.”
55.3: “Tomorrow I shall ascend into the highest shamayim, to the Yerushalayim above, where my everlasting inheritance awaits me.”
55.4: “Therefore I urge you to do everything pleasing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”

56.1: Methushelaḥ answered his father Ḥanoḵ, saying, “Father, what would please you for me to prepare in your presence, so that you may baraḵ our dwellings and your sons, and so that your people may receive esteem through you before you depart, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has commanded?”
56.2: Ḥanoḵ answered his son Methushelaḥ, “Listen, my child. From the time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 anointed me with the oil of His esteem, I have eaten no food. My being no longer longs for earthly pleasures, and I desire nothing from this earth.”

57.1: “My child Methushelaḥ, summon all your brothers, everyone in your household, and the elders of the people. I wish to speak with them before I depart, as has been appointed for me.”
57.2: Methushelaḥ hurried and gathered his brothers Regim, Riman, Uchan, Chermion, and Gaidad, together with all the elders of the people, before his father Ḥanoḵ. Then Ḥanoḵ baraḵ them and said:

58.2: “In those days 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came down to the earth for Aḏam’s sake and visited all His creatures. After creating them, He made Aḏam. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 called all the beasts of the earth, the creeping creatures, and the birds that fly through the air, and brought them before our father Aḏam.”
58.3: “Aḏam gave names to every living creature on the earth.”
58.4: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appointed him to rule over them all, placing them under his authority. He made them unable to speak and without human understanding, so that they would obey mankind and remain subject to him.”
58.5: “In the same way, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made each person master over his possessions.”
58.6: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 does not judge the being of an animal in place of a human being. Rather, He holds mankind accountable concerning the animals in this world, for mankind has a distinct place.”
58.7: “As each human being is counted, so the animals and their beings, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 created, shall not perish before the great judgment. They shall testify against those who mistreated them or failed to feed them properly.”

59.1: “Whoever defiles the life of an animal also defiles his own being.”
59.2: “For mankind brings clean animals as sacrifices for sin, seeking healing for his being.”
59.3: “When clean animals and birds are brought as sacrifices, a man seeks healing for his being.”
59.4: “Everything given to you for food, bind by its four feet so that the act of healing may be carried out properly.”
59.5: “But whoever kills an animal without binding it harms his own being and defiles his own flesh.”
59.6: “And whoever secretly harms any animal does evil and defiles his own being.”

6.1: They showed me the treasury of dew, which looked like olive oil and had the appearance of all the flowers of the earth. I also saw many messengers guarding the treasuries of these things and how they opened and closed them.

60.1: “Whoever takes the life of another person destroys his own being and his own body, and there is no healing for him forever.”
60.2: “Whoever sets a trap for another person shall be caught in it himself, and there is no healing for him forever.”
60.3: “Whoever lies in wait to harm another person in a matter of judgment shall not escape retribution at the great judgment.”
60.4: “Whoever acts deceitfully or speaks evil against another being shall never establish righteousness for himself.”

61.1: “Now, my children, keep your hearts from every injustice that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hates. As a person asks Elohim to care for his own being, so let him treat every living creature. I know that in the great age to come countless inheritances are prepared for mankind: good for those who do good and evil for those who do evil.”
61.2: “Ashrĕ are those who enter the good dwelling places, for in the evil ones there is neither peace nor a way of return.”
61.3: “Listen, my children, young and old! If a person vows to bring an offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from the work of his own hands, yet presents something his hands did not make, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will turn away from the work of his hands, and that person will gain nothing from his labor.”
61.4: “Even if his own hands performed the work, if he continually grumbles in his heart, he shall gain no benefit.”

62.1: “Ashrĕ is the man who patiently brings his offerings before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with faith, for he shall find forgiveness of sins.”
62.2: “But if he withdraws his promise before the appointed time, there is no repentance for him. And if the time passes without his willingly fulfilling what he promised, there is no repentance after death.”
62.3: “For every work a person offers before its proper time is deceit before mankind and sin before Elohim.”

63.1: “When a person clothes the naked and feeds the hungry, he shall receive a reward from Elohim.”
63.2: “But if he complains in his heart, he does double wrong: he harms himself and dishonors what he gives. He shall receive no reward for it.”
63.3: “If he fills himself with food and clothes his own body and shows contempt, he acts wickedly. He shall lose the fruit of his endurance of poverty and receive no reward for his good deeds.”
63.4: “Every proud and boastful person is hateful to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Every false word, clothed in deceit, shall be cut down by the sword of death and cast into the fire to burn forever.”

64.1: When Ḥanoḵ had spoken these words to his sons, people far and near heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was calling him. They consulted one another and said:
64.2: “Let us go and greet Ḥanoḵ with a kiss.” Two thousand men gathered and went to Achuzan, where Ḥanoḵ was staying with his sons.
64.3: The elders and the whole assembly came, bowed before Ḥanoḵ, embraced him, and said:
64.4: “Our father Ḥanoḵ, may you be baruḵ by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Now baraḵ your sons and all the people, so that we may be honored in your presence today.”
64.5: “For you shall be esteemed before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 forever. He has chosen you above all people on earth and appointed you to record all His creation, visible and invisible, and to be a redeemer from the sins of mankind and a helper to your household.”

65.1: Ḥanoḵ answered all the people, saying, “Listen, my children. Before any created thing existed, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 brought forth the visible and invisible things.”
65.2: “After much time had passed, He created man in the likeness of His own form. He gave him eyes to see, ears to hear, a heart to consider, and understanding with which to reason.”
65.3: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 observed all the deeds of mankind. He created all His creatures and divided time. He appointed years, divided the years into months, and the months into days, and established seven days in their cycle.”
65.4: “He also appointed the hours and measured them carefully, so that mankind might consider time and count the years, months, and hours, their changes, beginnings, and endings. Thus each person could count the days of his life from birth until death, reflect upon his sins, and record his good and evil deeds. Nothing is hidden from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Therefore let everyone know his deeds, keep His commands without transgression, and preserve what I have written from generation to generation.”
65.5: “When all visible and invisible creation reaches the end appointed by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, every person shall come before the great judgment. Then measured time shall pass away. Years, months, days, and hours shall no longer be counted, but shall be gathered together as one.”
65.6: “There shall be one everlasting age, and all the righteous who escape the great judgment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall be gathered into it. For them that great age shall begin, and they shall live forever. There shall be no labor, sickness, humiliation, anxiety, need, cruelty, night, or darkness among them, but only great light.”
65.7: “They shall have an immense, indestructible wall and a bright, everlasting paradise that cannot decay. All mortal and perishable things shall pass away, and everlasting life shall remain.”

66.1: “Now, my children, keep yourselves from every injustice that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hates.”
66.2: “Walk before Him with reverence and trembling, and serve Him alone.”
66.3: “Bow before the true Elohim, not before speechless idols. Honor His likeness and bring righteous offerings before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for He hates injustice.”
66.4: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sees all things. Whenever a person forms a thought in his heart, He knows and examines it. Every thought stands before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who established the earth and placed every creature upon it.”
66.5: “Look toward the shamayim, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is there. Consider the depths of the sea and everything beneath the earth, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is there also.”
66.6: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 created all things. Do not turn from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of all creation to bow before things made by human hands, for no deed can be hidden from Him.”
66.7: “Walk, my children, with patience, gentleness, honesty, faith, and truth. Remain steadfast through provocation, sorrow, reliance on promises, sickness, insults, injuries, temptations, nakedness, and need. Love one another until you depart from this troubled age and inherit the everlasting one.”
66.8: “Ashrĕ are the righteous who escape the great judgment. They shall shine seven times more brightly than the sun. In this present world, a seventh portion is taken from all things: light, darkness, food, pleasure, sorrow, paradise, torment, fire, frost, and everything else. All these things have been written down so that you may read and understand.”

67.1: After Ḥanoḵ had spoken to the people, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent darkness over the earth. It covered those who stood with Ḥanoḵ, and the messengers carried him into the highest shamayim, where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 dwells. He received Ḥanoḵ and placed him before His face. Then the darkness lifted, and light returned to the earth.
67.2: The people saw what had happened but did not understand how Ḥanoḵ had been taken away. They gave esteem to Elohim and found a scroll bearing the words, “The Invisible and Spiritual Elohim.” Then they returned to their homes.

68.1: Ḥanoḵ was born on the sixth day of the month Tsivan and lived three hundred and sixty-five years.
68.2: He was taken up into the shamayim on the first day of Tsivan and remained there for sixty days.
68.3: He recorded the signs of all creation that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had made and wrote three hundred and sixty-six books. He gave them to his sons and remained on earth for thirty days. Then he was taken up again into the shamayim on the sixth day of Tsivan, at the very day and hour of his birth.
68.4: As the nature of mankind in this life is hidden in darkness, so are the moments of conception, birth, and departure from this world.
68.5: At the hour he was conceived, he was born; and at that same hour, he departed this life.
68.6: Methushelaḥ and his brothers, all the sons of Ḥanoḵ, hurried to build an altar at Achuzan, the place from which Ḥanoḵ had been taken into the shamayim.
68.7: They brought oxen for sacrifice, gathered the people, and offered sacrifices before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
68.8: The elders and the whole assembly came to the feast and brought gifts to the sons of Ḥanoḵ.
68.9: They held a great feast and rejoiced for three days, praising Elohim for the sign He had given through Ḥanoḵ, who had found favor with Him. They resolved to pass down the account to their children, from generation to generation and age to age.

7.1: The men led me up into the second shamayim and showed me darkness deeper than any darkness on earth. There I saw prisoners hanging under guard, awaiting the great and boundless judgment. These messenger-spirits were darker than earthly darkness and wept without ceasing at every hour.
7.2: I asked the men with me, “Why are these beings tormented without ceasing?” They answered, “They are those who rebelled against Elohim. They did not obey His commands but followed their own will and turned away with their prince, who is also bound in the fifth shamayim.”
7.3: I felt great pity for them. They greeted me and said, “Man of Elohim, pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for us.” But I answered, “Who am I, a mortal man, to pray for messenger-spirits? Who knows where I am going or what will happen to me? And who will pray for me?”

8.1: The men took me from there and led me into the third shamayim. I looked down and saw the fruit of that place, whose goodness was beyond anything known on earth.
8.2: I saw trees covered with sweet-smelling blossoms and looked upon their fragrant fruit. All the food they produced gave off a delightful fragrance.
8.3: In the midst of those trees stood the tree of life, in the place where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rests when He enters paradise. Its goodness and fragrance are beyond description, and its beauty surpasses all other created things. On every side it gleams like gold, crimson, and fire. It spreads over everything and bears every kind of fruit.
8.4: Its root is in the garden at the end of the earth.
8.5: Paradise lies between what is perishable and what is imperishable.
8.6: Two springs flow from there, bringing forth honey and milk, while their sources also bring forth oil and wine. They divide into four streams, flow gently around the place, and descend into the paradise of Ĕḏen, between what is perishable and what is imperishable.
8.7: From there they flow throughout the earth, completing their circuits like the other elements.
8.8: There is no fruitless tree there, and every place is baruḵ.
8.9: Three hundred radiant messengers guard the garden. With unceasing, sweet songs and voices that never fall silent, they serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at every hour of every day.
8.10: I said, “How delightful this place is!” And the men said to me:

9.1: “This place, Ḥanoḵ, is prepared for the righteous: those who endure every kind of offense from those who trouble them; who turn their eyes away from wickedness; who judge rightly; who give bread to the hungry, clothe the naked, lift up those who have fallen, and help injured orphans; and who walk blamelessly before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and serve Him alone. This place is prepared for them as an everlasting inheritance.”
